# Requirements Quality Checklist: HA Switchboard Feature Completeness

**Purpose**: Review whether the feature-completeness requirements are complete,
clear, consistent, measurable, and ready for implementation and release review.
**Created**: 2026-09-20
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the speckit-checklist workflow
from the feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality artifact.
Mark an item [x] only when the reviewer determines that the written
requirement is satisfactory; [x] does not mean implementation is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are the App installation, Core integration setup, discovery, manual setup, and Assist selection requirements all present? [Completeness, Spec §US1, Spec §FR-001]
- [x] CHK002 Are read-only, native single-device, Jev-routed single-device, parameterized, clarification, confirmation, batch, fallback, and refusal outcomes represented as separate user-value requirements? [Completeness, Spec §US2-§US5, Spec §FR-004, Spec §FR-041]
- [x] CHK054 Does the specification explicitly define Home Assistant native Assist/Conversation handling as the first path for supported routine intents, with Jev reserved for gray-area routing and generic fallback reserved for unresolved/open-ended requests? [Architecture, Spec §FR-004, Spec §FR-041, Plan §Design Decisions]
- [x] CHK055 Does the fallback requirement state that generic OpenAI-compatible fallback runs only after native handling and Jev routing leave an eligible unresolved/open-ended request, and cannot silently replace a routine device-control path after transport failure? [Safety, Spec §FR-017, Spec §FR-041]
- [x] CHK056 Does the App configuration distinguish Jev provider selection/endpoint/model/key, fallback base URL/model/key, the Core gateway token, privacy mode, and profile refresh with user-facing descriptions rather than opaque option names? [Clarity, Spec §US7, Spec §FR-016-§FR-017]
  > Reviewer note: Closed. The specification now enumerates all 13 current App fields, including the separate Jev, fallback, gateway-token, privacy, and profile-refresh fields, using the labels/descriptions in `app/config.yaml`, `app/translations/en.yaml`, and `app/DOCS.md`.
- [x] CHK057 Does the local-development requirement preserve the existing Supervisor/Core volume by default and require a verified snapshot plus explicit confirmation before destructive reset? [Recovery, Spec §FR-030-§FR-032]
- [x] CHK003 Does the specification define both startup profile reconciliation and operator-initiated scanning rather than only periodic refresh? [Completeness, Spec §US6, Spec §FR-011-§FR-013]
- [x] CHK004 Are the App, Core integration, Supervisor, Assist, Jev, fallback providers, Web UI, standalone deployment, and release publisher boundaries each assigned responsibilities? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002-§FR-003, Spec §FR-017-§FR-029]
- [x] CHK005 Are user-facing configuration help, diagnostics, accessibility, and failure-state requirements included rather than treated as implementation polish? [Completeness, Spec §US7, Spec §FR-021-§FR-024]
- [x] CHK006 Are local fixture creation, volume preservation, bounded E2E behavior, public packaging, and live release evidence included? [Completeness, Spec §US10, Spec §FR-031-§FR-040]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK007 Is “feature complete” bounded by the documented end-to-end journey and separated from external HACS/App repository acceptance? [Clarity, Spec §Definition of Done, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK008 Are “bounded,” “current,” “fresh,” “sanitized,” “safe,” and “actionable” defined through observable limits or states? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-014, Spec §FR-020, Spec §SC-002, Spec §SC-006]
- [x] CHK009 Is the maximum batch size stated consistently as 32 across multi-device behavior, contracts, plan, and assumptions? [Clarity, Consistency, Spec §US3, Spec §FR-008, Plan §Design Decisions]
- [x] CHK010 Does the specification distinguish fallback prose from a typed proposal and state what each may authorize? [Clarity, Spec §US5, Spec §FR-017-§FR-019]
- [x] CHK011 Are the prohibited generic refusal wording and the required reason-specific response behavior stated without conflicting response requirements? [Clarity, Spec §US2, Spec §FR-005, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK012 Are the terms “complete profile,” “active revision,” “partial batch,” and “one-level handoff” defined well enough for independent reviewers to reach the same interpretation? [Clarity, Spec §US3, Spec §US6, Spec §US5, Data Model]

## Consistency and Traceability

- [x] CHK013 Do the functional requirements align with the constitutional rule that Core alone owns Home Assistant execution? [Consistency, Constitution §I, Spec §FR-002-§FR-003]
- [x] CHK014 Do the fallback requirements preserve the same allowlist, freshness, parameter, confirmation, idempotency, execution, and verification gates as Jev? [Consistency, Constitution §II, Spec §FR-018-§FR-019, Contract provider-routing]
- [x] CHK015 Do the profile atomicity requirements agree across invalidation, manual scan, startup, restart, and failure scenarios? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011-§FR-014, Contract profile-reconciliation]
- [x] CHK016 Do App option requirements consistently require a real behavior, safe default, migration path, and documentation? [Consistency, Spec §US9, Spec §FR-016, Research Decision 7]
  > Reviewer note: Closed. The active schema is `adapter_only`; legacy `supervisor_read_only` is normalized at option load to `adapter_only` with `supervisor_read_only_migrated_to_adapter_only`, and no read-only mode remains as an active schema choice.
- [x] CHK017 Do the success criteria map to the user stories and avoid claiming that source/CI success alone proves live behavior? [Consistency, Spec §SC-001-§SC-012, Constitution §IV, Plan §Release]
- [x] CHK018 Is every requirement that crosses the App/Core/provider boundary, including the native Assist fast path, represented by a corresponding contract or acceptance scenario? [Traceability, Spec §FR-001-§FR-041, contracts/]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK019 Can the installation success criterion be evaluated without relying on an undocumented YAML edit or manual file copy? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §US1, Spec §SC-001]
- [x] CHK020 Can profile startup and manual-scan timing be objectively measured for both success and bounded failure? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002, Spec §SC-006]
- [x] CHK021 Can a reviewer determine whether every acceptance-matrix write had a current revision, valid capability, confirmation, idempotency decision, and verification? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003-§SC-005]
- [x] CHK022 Are secret/redaction outcomes stated as observable properties of both provider payloads and diagnostics? [Measurability, Spec §FR-018, Spec §FR-023, Spec §SC-004]
- [x] CHK023 Are restart/upgrade preservation expectations quantified by cycles and named state? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007]
- [x] CHK024 Are release success criteria specific about version, revision, architecture, mirror, tag, and mandatory gates? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §FR-036-§FR-040, Spec §SC-010]

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK025 Are primary success flows documented for both a fresh installation and an existing installation upgrade? [Scenario Coverage, Spec §US1, Spec §US10]
- [x] CHK026 Are alternate setup flows documented for Supervisor discovery failure and manual endpoint/token entry? [Alternate Flow, Spec §US1]
- [x] CHK027 Are exception flows documented for stale profiles, unavailable targets, invalid parameters, malformed provider results, and provider outages? [Exception Flow, Spec §US2, Spec §US4, Spec §US5, Spec §US6]
- [x] CHK028 Are recovery flows documented for App restart, Core restart, reconnect, failed replacement, token rotation, and release rollback? [Recovery, Spec §US6, Spec §US9, Spec §US10]
- [x] CHK029 Are multi-user and multi-conversation boundaries explicit for clarification and confirmation? [Scenario Coverage, Spec §US4, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK030 Are local-only, Jev-hosted, and hosted-fallback privacy paths distinct in the requirements? [Scenario Coverage, Spec §US5, Spec §FR-017-§FR-018]
- [x] CHK031 Are both App deployment and standalone Compose deployment represented with their different security boundaries? [Scenario Coverage, Spec §US9, Spec §FR-027-§FR-029]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK032 Are incomplete, oversized, duplicate, malformed, and generation-racing snapshots addressed without allowing partial activation? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases, Spec §FR-014]
- [x] CHK033 Are duplicate requests, toggle replay, partial batch failure, and unavailable batch members addressed with distinct outcomes? [Edge Case, Spec §US3, Spec §FR-006-§FR-008]
- [x] CHK034 Are missing, invalid, out-of-range, conflicting, and expired parameter values addressed? [Edge Case, Spec §US4, Spec §FR-009]
- [x] CHK035 Are expired, consumed, cancelled, cross-user, and cross-conversation pending contexts prevented from authorizing a write? [Edge Case, Spec §US4, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK036 Are unsafe redirects, invalid provider schemas, excessive latency, rate limits, circuit state, and handoff loops addressed? [Edge Case, Spec §US5, Spec §FR-020]
- [x] CHK037 Are empty options, unreadable Supervisor options, AppArmor differences, and interrupted local rebuilds addressed? [Edge Case, Spec §US9, Spec §US10, Spec §FR-030-§FR-032]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK038 Are security requirements explicit about least privilege, non-root execution, AppArmor, ingress restriction, gateway-token separation, and absence of broad Home Assistant API access? [Security, Constitution §Security and Product Boundaries, Spec §FR-027-§FR-028]
- [x] CHK039 Are privacy requirements explicit about credentials, raw entity IDs, raw utterances, unrestricted service data, and provider response bodies? [Privacy, Spec §FR-018, Spec §FR-023, Spec §FR-026]
- [x] CHK040 Are request size, profile size, log retention, batch size, timeout, retry, handoff, and response bounds either quantified or assigned to a reviewed policy value? [NFR, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-020, Spec §SC-002, Plan §Technical Context]
  > Reviewer note: Closed. The specification now records the reviewed values from `app/ha_switchboard/limits.py` and the Jev/OpenAI-compatible fallback adapters, including request/response bytes, profile/event retention, batch, timeout, retry, rate, and one-level handoff bounds.
- [x] CHK041 Are Web UI keyboard, focus, accessible-name, reduced-motion, and non-color-only status requirements stated for every operator control? [Accessibility, Spec §US7, Spec §FR-024]
- [x] CHK042 Are availability and recovery expectations distinguished from liveness and readiness? [NFR, Spec §US7, Spec §FR-015, Spec §FR-022]
- [x] CHK043 Are performance goals compatible with provider timeout and Home Assistant verification latency rather than implying an unbounded SLA? [NFR, Spec §SC-002, Spec §SC-006, Plan §Technical Context]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [x] CHK044 Are Home Assistant Core, Supervisor, Assist, HACS, provider, Docker/Podman, and public registry dependencies identified with ownership? [Dependencies, Spec §Assumptions, Research §Open external dependencies]
- [x] CHK045 Is the assumption that Home Assistant batches are not transactional reflected in partial-result requirements and rollback guidance? [Assumption, Spec §US3, Spec §Assumptions, Contract conversation-execution]
- [x] CHK046 Is the OpenRouter Decisions parameter-extraction limitation identified as a provider-contract dependency rather than silently promised? [Dependency, Spec §US4, Research §Decision 3]
- [x] CHK047 Is the supported Home Assistant capability matrix clearly separated from future compatibility targets and unsupported surfaces? [Scope, Spec §US8, Spec §FR-025, Spec §FR-039]
- [x] CHK048 Are the local volume-preservation and destructive-reset assumptions reflected in both requirements and validation guidance? [Assumption, Spec §FR-032, Quickstart]

## Ambiguities and Conflicts

- [x] CHK049 Is the migration/removal decision for supervisor_read_only resolved before implementation begins, with no option left as an undocumented no-op? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-016, Research §Decision 7]
  > Reviewer note: Closed. The final choice is legacy migration to `adapter_only` with the explicit compatibility warning; `supervisor_read_only` is excluded from the current schema and no read-only adapter is claimed.
- [x] CHK050 Is the distinction between a route compatibility check and a real user request clear enough to avoid unintended provider cost or device action? [Ambiguity, Spec §US5, Contract diagnostics-webui]
- [x] CHK051 Are “other supported domains” either enumerated in the matrix or explicitly excluded before release acceptance? [Ambiguity, Spec §US8, Spec §FR-025]
  > Reviewer note: Closed. The specification enumerates the executable domains (`light`, `switch`, `fan`, `media_player`, `climate`, `lock`, `cover`, `garage`) and explicitly excludes script/scene activation plus unsupported domains, operations, and service shapes.
- [x] CHK052 Are external HACS/App repository acceptance outcomes represented as pending dependencies rather than implementation promises? [Conflict, Spec §Definition of Done, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK053 Do the requirements avoid conflicting goals between retaining a last valid read profile and blocking writes when freshness or authorization is uncertain? [Consistency, Spec §US6, Spec §FR-014, Spec §FR-030]

## Notes

- Checked items indicate that the requirements question is satisfied by the
  reviewed artifacts; they do not claim that implementation or runtime
  validation is complete. Unchecked items retain the adjacent reviewer note
  where the written requirements remain ambiguous or incomplete.
- References point to the feature specification, constitution, plan, data model,
  contracts, or quickstart so reviewers can trace each quality question.
- The built-in checklists/requirements.md file remains the specification
  authoring checklist and has a separate lifecycle.
